It involves creating a small hole in your abdomen, called a stoma, which allows urine to pass through a catheter and be collected in a bag that you will wear on your abdomen or under your clothing.

The procedure itself is relatively quick and can be done as an outpatient procedure. You will be given medication to help you relax and a local anesthetic to numb the area where the catheter will be inserted. Once the catheter is in place, you will be able to feel the catheter drainage bag against your abdomen.

Once the catheter is in place, you will need to learn how to care for it. This will involve emptying the catheter bag regularly, keeping the area around the catheter clean, and monitoring the catheter for any signs of infection.

I know that this can be a big change, but it's important to remember that it will improve your quality of life and give you greater independence. Many people find that they are able to return to work and other activities they enjoy once they have adapted to the catheter.

I'm here to answer any questions you may have, and I can also connect you with a urologist who can help you decide if this is the right choice for you. If you have any concerns or questions, please don't hesitate to reach out.
